findings.highlight: two hours since I carried Sakura in
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を居間に運んでから二時間
findings.governingReading: Two hours have passed since Shirou carried Sakura from near the gate into the living room.
findings.explanation: The English omits the living room as the destination.

findings.highlight: Function is finally returning to my numbed mind
findings.evidenceJa: 寝起きで麻痺していたこっちの頭も、ようやくまともに回り始めていた
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s head, numb from waking, has finally begun functioning properly.
findings.explanation: The English omits the waking cause and renders recovery in awkward, less definite terms.

findings.highlight: I’m fine now
findings.evidenceJa: なんとかまともには戻った
findings.governingReading: Shirou has somehow returned to something approaching normal.
findings.explanation: The English overstates partial, qualified recovery as being fine.

findings.highlight: you just sat down
findings.evidenceJa: ペタンって床に座っただけ
findings.governingReading: Illya says Shirou simply plopped down flat on the floor.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the floor and the abrupt collapsed manner.

findings.highlight: she took Sakura to her room
findings.evidenceJa: 桜を客間に連れて行った
findings.governingReading: Rin appears to have taken Sakura to the guest room.
findings.explanation: The English changes the shared guest room into Sakura’s own room.

findings.highlight: checking out the closet
findings.evidenceJa: 和室のクローゼットを調べてた
findings.governingReading: Illya saw Rin checking the closet in the Japanese-style room.
findings.explanation: The English omits the room that identifies which clothes Rin could be seeking.

findings.highlight: My body remembers that I’ve been pondering that problem for all that time
findings.evidenceJa: イヤというほど追究したと、記憶していた体が訴えている
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s remembering body insists that he pursued the question more than enough to become sick of it throughout the missing interval.
findings.explanation: The English keeps bodily memory but removes its insistent agency and the oppressive excess of repetition.

findings.highlight: even if you try to find what’s not there
findings.evidenceJa: 無いものをいくら掘り出しても
findings.governingReading: Illya compares searching absent memory to repeatedly digging for something that no longer exists.
findings.explanation: The English removes the excavation image and its futile persistence.

findings.highlight: I don’t know
findings.evidenceJa: さあ
findings.governingReading: Rin answers with a distancing “Who knows?” before directing Shirou to Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English changes rhetorical refusal into a direct claim of ignorance.

findings.highlight: head to Sakura’s room
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の客間へ足を向けた
findings.governingReading: Shirou heads toward the guest room where Sakura is resting.
findings.explanation: The English again makes it Sakura’s own room.

findings.highlight: Sakura is breathing hard
findings.evidenceJa: ベッドの上
findings.governingReading: Sakura greets Shirou from the bed.
findings.explanation: The English omits her position and begins instead with her breathing.

findings.highlight: Sakura is breathing hard
findings.evidenceJa: 少し苦しげな息遣い
findings.governingReading: Sakura speaks with breathing that sounds slightly labored.
findings.explanation: The English intensifies the qualified symptom into breathing hard.

findings.highlight: I’ll go anywhere for you
findings.evidenceJa: 何処にいたってやってくる
findings.governingReading: Wherever Shirou happens to be, he will come when Sakura collapses.
findings.explanation: The English changes a condition on his location into a sweeping promise to go anywhere for her.

findings.highlight: it’s me that should be treating you
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の看病は俺の役目
findings.governingReading: Shirou calls looking after or nursing Sakura his role.
findings.explanation: The English turns domestic care into medical treatment.

findings.highlight: I try to sit level with Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 横になった桜と視線をできるだけ合わせる
findings.governingReading: Shirou positions himself to meet the reclining Sakura’s gaze as directly as possible.
findings.explanation: The English moves the alignment from their eyes to the height of his seated body.

findings.highlight: No. She said I should ask you
findings.evidenceJa: ああ。訊きたい事は全部桜に訊けとさ
findings.governingReading: Shirou affirms Sakura’s observation and reports Rin told him to ask Sakura everything.
findings.explanation: The English begins with the opposite response.

findings.highlight: we can’t manage
findings.evidenceJa: 身が持たないだろ、俺も桜も
findings.governingReading: Shirou says neither he nor Sakura could physically or emotionally endure Rin being severe at all times.
findings.explanation: The English removes both named experiencers and weakens endurance to generic management.

findings.highlight: Her satisfied expression
findings.evidenceJa: 心底満足そうな笑顔
findings.governingReading: Sakura wears a smile that looks satisfied from the bottom of her heart.
findings.explanation: The English removes the wholehearted degree and reduces the smile to an expression.

findings.highlight: I’m just exhausted
findings.evidenceJa: 体力の低下
findings.governingReading: Sakura reports reduced physical strength.
findings.explanation: The English changes diminished capacity into temporary exhaustion and adds minimizing “just.”

findings.highlight: this is something I have to know
findings.evidenceJa: そうであってもらわないと困る
findings.governingReading: Shirou not only needs to check her magical energy; he needs the answer to be that she has enough.
findings.explanation: The English omits the required positive result.

findings.highlight: I roll up my sleeve in a show of confidence
findings.evidenceJa: 右手を腕まくりして桜を元気づける
findings.governingReading: Shirou rolls up his right sleeve to cheer or encourage Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English omits the right side and changes his purpose into displaying confidence.

findings.highlight: I hate that I can’t even do that
findings.evidenceJa: そんなコトもできないなんて、悔しいです
findings.governingReading: Sakura finds her inability to help painfully frustrating.
findings.explanation: The English changes frustrated grief into hatred of the situation.

findings.highlight: Sakura is concerned about her role
findings.evidenceJa: 桜は“自分の役割”に拘っている
findings.governingReading: Sakura is fixated on or clings to her assigned role.
findings.explanation: The English reduces psychologically rigid attachment to concern.

findings.highlight: tries to be the normal Matou Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 今まで通りの間桐桜であろうとする
findings.governingReading: Sakura tries at least to remain Matou Sakura as she has been until now.
findings.explanation: The English turns continuity of identity into a judgment of normality.

findings.highlight: she can’t even manage something as simple as that
findings.evidenceJa: 些細なコトさえ、桜には許されない
findings.governingReading: Now even that small role is not permitted to Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English changes deprivation and denial into personal incapacity.

findings.highlight: A sick person has to rest like one
findings.evidenceJa: 病人は病人らしく休まないと損だぞ
findings.governingReading: Shirou jokes that a sick person loses out unless she rests like one.
findings.explanation: The English removes the comic loss-or-benefit logic.

findings.highlight: I jokingly say what I plan to do
findings.evidenceJa: 冗談っぽく、本気で今後の方針を口にする
findings.governingReading: Shirou states his genuine future policy in a joking manner.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the joking delivery but omits that the commitment is sincere.

findings.highlight: I won’t do anything for at least half a year
findings.evidenceJa: 半年は大人しくしてる
findings.governingReading: Shirou promises to stay out of Sakura’s kitchen or behave quietly for six months.
findings.explanation: The English overstates this as doing nothing at all.

findings.highlight: unless I’m holding a pan or something
findings.evidenceJa: 少しは鍋を持たないと落ち着かない
findings.governingReading: After nearly eight years in the kitchen, Shirou cannot settle without handling a cooking pot at least a little.
findings.explanation: The English changes the pot and adds dismissive uncertainty about the object.

findings.highlight: Please eat my meals once I get well
findings.evidenceJa: 真っ先にごはんを食べてくださいね
findings.governingReading: Sakura asks Shirou to eat her food first of all once she recovers.
findings.explanation: The English omits the priority that makes this the first promised act after recovery.

findings.highlight: I stop at the door
findings.evidenceJa: ドアノブに手をかけ
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks his final question with his hand on the doorknob.
findings.explanation: The English removes the concrete departure posture.

findings.highlight: I woke up early
findings.evidenceJa: 先に目が覚めたから
findings.governingReading: Sakura claims she woke before Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English changes relative waking order into an absolute early time.

findings.highlight: She replies as naturally as I asked her
findings.evidenceJa: 俺と同じぐらい、自然な明るさで返答した
findings.governingReading: Sakura replies with a natural brightness matching the degree of Shirou’s deliberately natural question.
findings.explanation: The English preserves apparent naturalness but removes brightness and the measured mirroring of their performances.
